name: Reversible database migration
description: Design and verify a backwards-compatible database migration with restore evidence, observable rollout, and explicit data boundaries.

outcomes.description: The schema change has an ordered migration path, compatibility window, and tested constraints.
A receipt names a restorable snapshot or export and the post-change verification result.

prerequisites.description: Current and target schema shape, data ownership, constraints, and indexes are understood.
prerequisites.check: Review metadata and list reads and writes affected by the change.

prerequisites.description: A restorable snapshot or export exists before any destructive or irreversible operation.
prerequisites.check: Verify restore metadata without copying data values into the lane.

lanes.objective: Describe current shape, target shape, compatibility order, and restore plan.
Write the bounded migration and safe compatibility checks for the target schema.
Run isolated apply, compatibility, constraint, and restore-route checks.

qualityGates.description: Reads and writes remain compatible for the declared rollout window.
The snapshot or export and restore route are identifiable before applying a risky step.
Constraints, indexes, data shape, and post-change checks pass without exposing values.

ownerConfirmationBoundaries.action: Enter a password, one-time code, passkey, or challenge response for a database check.
ownerConfirmationBoundaries.boundary: Stop and hand the entry to the owner; use an approved safe session or isolated fixture instead.
ownerConfirmationBoundaries.reason: Authentication material is a human-only boundary.

ownerConfirmationBoundaries.action: Apply destructive schema or data work, billing or account-security changes, or live financial behavior.
ownerConfirmationBoundaries.boundary: Stop before the action and obtain one explicit owner confirmation for that individual action.
ownerConfirmationBoundaries.reason: A migration must prove reversal before live data impact.

rollbackRescue.rollbackPlan: Use the verified restore route or a forward-compatible corrective migration; never discard data to hide an incomplete check.
rescueSteps: Preserve migration and restore metadata without values.
Stop at the first incompatible read or write.
Record whether the migration was merged, abandoned, or safely reversed.
stopConditions: No restorable snapshot or export is identifiable.
Compatibility cannot be demonstrated in isolation.
A protected owner boundary is reached.

redactionRules: Never include database values, credentials, tokens, or private connection paths.
Name schema objects and migration identifiers only.
